item.title: Salsa Bachata Classes and Social at The Albion — Fri Nov 13, 7:00 PM — The Albion Rooftop & Club
item.description:
FREE Salsa & Bachata classes every Friday at The Albion in South Melbourne! FREE Latin dance classes and social dancing as the pre-party to the Oye Latino Reggaeton night EVERY FRIDAY at The Albion Rooftop & Club! 172 York Street South Melbourne 6:45pm Doors open. Come in for a drink & meet the other students 7pm Salsa classes levels 1 & 2 8pm Bachata classes levels 1 & 2 First-timers welcome! 9pm Salsa & Bachata social dancing until about 10:15pm 10:15pm the Reggaeton DJs start the Oye Latino party and play a mix of Latin hits until 4 or 5am! 10:30pm head upstairs to the rooftop for more Bachata & Salsa mixed in with some Latin favourites, Reggaeton, Afrobeats, R&B and more! FREE ENTRY ALL NIGHT! Tickets are not compulsory but it does help us manage male & female ratios for the dance classes and so the venue knows how many staff they need! item.title: LATIN PARADISE SALSA & BACHATA MONTHLY PARTY — Fri Nov 13, 8:00 PM — Crofton Hall Orpington
item.description: Learn Salsa, learn Bachata! Have fun and meet new friends!​ Our regular Fridays become a party on the Second Friday of every month. Join us at our Bromley Special Salsa & Bachata Party, hosted at Bromley United Services Club, Bromley, with plenty of free street parking available. We kick off the night with Salsa & Bachata lessons. If you’re new to dancing, we recommend joining our beginners’ group. All levels are welcome! No prior experience or dance partner is needed. Many attendees come solo, and we rotate partners throughout the lesson, giving you the chance to dance with different people. If you’d prefer to stay with your own partner for the entire class, just let the teacher know, and we’ll be happy to accommodate you. Since most Latin parties feature both Salsa and Bachata, learning both is not only fun but also a must! So, we strongly recommend and encourage our students to learn both. SCHEDULE: 7pm to 8pm: Cuban Salsa: Beginners – Improvers – Intermediate 8pm to 9pm:

item.title: 🌰 Hogg’s Hollow Fall Walk & Lunch! 🍂! — Sun Nov 22, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 15 Years! ### 🌰 Hogg’s Hollow Fall Walk & Lunch! 🍂
Join us for a beautiful fall walk through Hogg’s Hollow, one of Toronto’s charming historic neighbourhoods tucked away in North York. With its winding roads, forested trails, stone bridges, and scenic ravines, this area feels like a hidden village in the middle of the city — especially when the leaves turn golden and the air starts to feel like autumn.
We’ll explore the valley around the Don River West Branch, taking in the neighbourhood’s natural beauty and historic character. Along the way, we’ll touch on the story of James Hogg, the Scottish settler associated with the area’s early mill, and the tragic **Hogg’s Hollow Disaster of 1960**, when five workers lost their lives during tunnel construction.
After our walk, we’ll head to **Swiss Chalet** for lunch, because nothing says fall like comfort food and good company! 🍗

item.title: Tubman Talks Roundtable: Decolonizing Knowledge Production in Ituri, North and South Kivu Provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo: Extractivism, Environmental Governance, Gender Justice, and Community Knowledge — Thu Nov 26, 2:00 PM
item.description: Date: Thursday, November 26, 2026 Time: 2:00-3:30pm EST Location: Virtual Register here: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/z7joamFfT3aKIAIwCsVaEw Title: Decolonizing Knowledge Production in Ituri, North and South Kivu Provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo: Extractivism, Environmental Governance, Gender Justice, and Community Knowledge Abstract The provinces of Ituri, North and South Kivu in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) are shaped by complex intersections of resource extraction, environmental governance, armed conflict, gendered violence, and community resistance. Yet dominant institutional and external frameworks often produce knowledge about these realities in ways that marginalize local experiences, Indigenous and community-based knowledge, and the intellectual contributions of Congolese women. This presentation examines the possibilities and challenges of decolonizing knowledge production by centering locally grounded research, lived experiences, and community
